newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville limits Thurs offers to non-firm power.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville limits Thurs offers to non-firm power.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) refrained from offering firm power for Thursday pre-schedulings, but continued to offer non-firm during both peak and off-peak hours, the agency said Wednesday.
BPA also lowered its price offers for off-peak non-firm power by $1.50 to $2.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Wednesday pre-schedulings.
"We are uncertain about constraints we might see for flood control. If we have extra power we will sell it real-time," said a trade source at the Portland, Ore.-based agency.
Thursday non-firm power for hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 PST was offered at $16.00 per MWh for both Northwest and California-Oregon border (COB) deliveries, compared with $17.50 for Wednesdasy.
Non-firm offers for hours ending 0600-2300 PST was offered at $18.00, down from $20.00.
Prices for non-firm power during peak demand hours ending 0700-2200 PST were unchanged at $22.50 for the Northwest and $23.50 for COB.
BPA also continued to limit peak sales to 500 MW.
